evaluated.name: CashFundedInnovation
evaluated.expression: MUL(RANK(RATIO(COALESCE(xrd, 0), at)), RANK(NEG(RATIO(SUB(ib, oancf), at))))
evaluated.hypothesis: Firms that invest heavily in R&D *and* report earnings backed by cash (low total accruals) are making genuine intangible investment, while high-R&D firms whose earnings rest on accruals are managing reported results; only the former are systematically underpriced.
evaluated.reasoning: Multiplying the two rank channels makes the signal high only in the joint corner (high intangible intensity AND clean accruals), so it is not a monotone re-labeling of either single-theme sort. Expensed R&D depresses book earnings while low accruals confirm the depressed earnings are real cash, a combination that mispricing models predict should earn positive drift.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: GoodwillWeightedAccrualAggression
evaluated.expression: MUL(RATIO(SUB(ib, oancf), at), RANK(RATIO(COALESCE(gdwl, 0), at)))
evaluated.hypothesis: Accruals are most toxic in firms whose intangible base is acquired (goodwill) rather than organically generated, since purchase accounting supplies discretionary allocations and deferred impairments that amplify accrual-based earnings inflation.
evaluated.reasoning: The goodwill rank acts as an intensity weight on the accrual channel, so pure high-accrual firms with no acquired intangibles get muted scores while acquisitive, accrual-inflated firms are pushed to the short leg. This isolates the accounting-driven component of intangible-related earnings from productive internal investment.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: InnovationAccelVsAccrualBuildup
evaluated.expression: SUMRANK(ACCEL(RATIO(COALESCE(xrd, 0), sale)), NEG(DELTA(RATIO(SUB(ib, oancf), at), 1)))
evaluated.hypothesis: A firm accelerating real intangible investment while simultaneously reducing its accrual intensity is shifting toward genuine growth; the reverse pattern (decelerating R&D, rising accruals) signals earnings propped up by accounting.
evaluated.reasoning: Using second differences in R&D intensity and first differences in accruals makes the signal about the direction of change in the investment/accounting mix rather than static intensity levels, which are already spanned by known factors. The divergence between real-investment momentum and accrual momentum is the cleanest separation of productive from cosmetic earnings dynamics.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: AccrualInnovationRotation
evaluated.expression: SUB(TS_RANK(RATIO(SUB(ib, oancf), at), 5), TS_RANK(RATIO(ADD(COALESCE(xrd, 0), COALESCE(intan, 0)), at), 5))
evaluated.hypothesis: What matters is the firm's internal rotation between real intangible investment and accounting-generated earnings: a firm sitting near the top of its own five-year accrual history while sitting near the bottom of its own intangible-intensity history is substituting accruals for investment, and its earnings will not persist.
evaluated.reasoning: Both channels are within-firm time-series ranks, so the signal is orthogonal to the cross-sectional level effects of Sloan accruals and R&D intensity and instead identifies a change in the firm's earnings-production mix, differencing out firm-level accounting technology and industry conventions. High values flag firms whose reported income is drifting toward accrual sources exactly when their intangible base is being starved, a combination the market should re-price downward as the accruals reverse.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: CashGrossProfitOnIntangibleCapital
evaluated.expression: RATIO(SUB(SUB(revt, cogs), SUB(ib, oancf)), ADD(at, TS_SUM(COALESCE(xrd, 0), 5)))
evaluated.hypothesis: Productive intangible investment should show up as cash-realized gross profit per dollar of true (tangible plus capitalized-intangible) capital; stripping accruals out of the profit numerator and adding the R&D stock to the capital base separates firms whose intangible spending actually earns a return from those whose profitability is an accrual artifact.
evaluated.reasoning: The numerator converts gross profit to a cash basis by removing the accrual wedge, and the denominator restates the invested-capital base to include off-balance-sheet intangible capital, so the ratio is an intangible-capital return on cash profits rather than an additive blend of two anomalies. It penalizes high-accrual "profitable" firms and high-R&D firms whose intangible stock generates no cash gross margin, while rewarding cheap, cash-productive innovators.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: IntangibleOpacityGatedAccrual
evaluated.expression: MUL(IND_ZSCORE(WINSOR(NEG(RATIO(SUB(ib, oancf), at)), 1)), IND_RANK(RATIO(ADD(COALESCE(xrd, 0), COALESCE(xad, 0)), sale)))
evaluated.hypothesis: The accrual mispricing is not uniform across firms: it is strongest where intangible spending (R&D plus advertising) makes reported earnings hardest to interpret, so the accrual signal should be amplified for intangible-opaque firms and switched off for transparent, tangible-asset firms.
evaluated.reasoning: The industry z-scored, winsorized accrual quality term carries the sign while the industry rank of intangible intensity acts as a bounded [0,1] amplification gate, producing a true moderation structure rather than an equal-weight difference of two standalone anomalies. Both legs are industry-neutral, so the signal does not proxy for sector membership, and adding advertising broadens the opacity proxy beyond R&D-reporting firms, which supports coverage.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: InnovationWorkingCapitalDiscipline
evaluated.expression: MUL(RANK(RATIO(COALESCE(xrd, 0), at)), RANK(RATIO(ADD(recch, invch), at)))
evaluated.hypothesis: For intangible-intensive firms the informative accrual component is the operating working-capital build (receivables and inventory), because revenue from new products is where channel-stuffing and premature recognition occur; R&D-heavy firms that grow without building receivables or inventory have genuine demand.
evaluated.reasoning: This decomposes the accrual leg rather than using the aggregate ib−oancf wedge, isolating which accrual component actually interacts with intangible intensity — a design question gen 0 never tested. Cash-flow-statement components are positive when working capital releases cash, so the joint high-rank corner is exactly "high innovation with clean revenue quality."
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: AcquiredIntangibleAccrualFlow
evaluated.expression: MUL(RANK(RATIO(SUB(ib, oancf), at)), RANK(RATIO(DELTA(COALESCE(intan, 0), 1), at)))
evaluated.hypothesis: The damaging combination is contemporaneous: firms booking large additions to acquired intangibles while simultaneously reporting accrual-heavy earnings are using purchase accounting and allocation discretion to manufacture income that later reverses through impairment.
evaluated.reasoning: Gen 0's goodwill-level weighting produced the best cross-sectional slope but a modest alpha, partly because the large mass of zero-goodwill firms compressed the short leg; switching to the intangible-addition flow and ranking both legs spreads firms across the sort and dates the mechanism to the acquisition year. It changes the economic channel from "stock of acquired intangibles" to "acquisition-year accounting discretion."
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: IntangibleAccrualInstability
evaluated.expression: MUL(RANK(VOL(RATIO(SUB(ib, oancf), at), 5)), RANK(RATIO(ADD(COALESCE(xrd, 0), COALESCE(xad, 0)), sale)))
evaluated.hypothesis: Opacity compounds: firms with high intangible spending whose accruals are also unstable year to year have the least interpretable earnings, and their reported profitability is accounting-driven rather than investment-driven, leading to negative drift.
evaluated.reasoning: This tests a second-moment (earnings-quality) channel rather than a level channel, which no gen-0 signal did, and it makes a falsifiable prediction that intangible intensity flips from good to bad once accrual reliability is poor. If it works, it tells us the positive R&D leg in CashFundedInnovation is really an earnings-quality effect in disguise.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: InnovationFundingGapAccrual
evaluated.expression: MUL(RANK(RATIO(SUB(COALESCE(xrd, 0), oancf), at)), RANK(RATIO(SUB(ib, oancf), at)))
evaluated.hypothesis: Innovation that outruns internally generated cash must be financed externally or sustained by accounting income; firms whose R&D exceeds operating cash flow *and* whose reported earnings rest on accruals are the clearest cases of accounting-driven rather than productive intangible investment, and their earnings reverse.
evaluated.reasoning: This introduces a financing channel absent from the archive — the intangible leg is no longer an intensity level but a cash-shortfall gap (xrd minus oancf), which is economically meaningful only jointly with how much of reported income is accrued. It predicts the short leg directly (cash-short innovators reporting accrual income) rather than averaging a profitability sort with an intensity sort, and both legs are ranked so the interaction is a genuine joint-corner condition rather than a scaling artifact.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: HiddenEquityCleanAccruals
evaluated.expression: MUL(RANK(RATIO(TS_SUM(COALESCE(xrd, 0), 5), ceq)), RANK(NEG(WINSOR(RATIO(SUB(ib, oancf), at), 1))))
evaluated.hypothesis: Expensing R&D leaves a stock of intangible capital off the balance sheet, so reported book equity understates true invested capital; among firms whose earnings are cash-backed rather than accrual-supported, this hidden-equity understatement is a genuine valuation distortion the market corrects slowly.
evaluated.reasoning: Scaling the five-year R&D stock by reported book equity measures how badly the balance sheet misstates capital — a book-based value channel distinct from an R&D/assets intensity sort and not spanned by HML, which uses the unadjusted book number. Gating it on accrual cleanliness is essential: hidden equity is only credible when the accompanying earnings are not themselves an accounting construct, which is exactly the productive-versus-accounting separation the theme requires.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: SustainedRnDRampCleanAccruals
evaluated.expression: MUL(RANK(TREND(RATIO(COALESCE(xrd, 0), at), 5)), RANK(NEG(WINSOR(RATIO(SUB(ib, oancf), at), 1))))
evaluated.hypothesis: Commitment to intangible investment is revealed by a sustained multi-year ramp in R&D intensity, not by a single-year level or a reporting dummy; firms steadily raising intangible investment while keeping earnings cash-backed are building real capability, whereas a rising accrual base alongside flat investment signals managed earnings.
evaluated.reasoning: Replacing the tie-saturated TS_COUNT dummy with a five-year TREND yields a continuous, well-spread commitment measure in which non-R&D firms sit at the middle (zero slope) rather than at an artificial extreme, fixing the degeneracy the critic identified. The five-year slope also avoids the noise that killed the earlier ACCEL construction, so it tests the persistence-versus-level design question with a statistically usable estimator.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: IntangibleAccrualNoisePremium
evaluated.expression: MUL(RANK(RATIO(ADD(COALESCE(xrd, 0), COALESCE(xad, 0)), sale)), RANK(ABS(WINSOR(RATIO(SUB(ib, oancf), at), 1))))
evaluated.hypothesis: For intangible-intensive firms the accrual leg prices information opacity, not earnings quality: large accruals of either sign make the already hard-to-value intangible firm even harder to value, and investors demand compensation for holding it.
evaluated.reasoning: This is the direct test implied by the gen-1 sign flip — replacing signed accruals with accrual magnitude separates "accounting-noise premium" from "clean-earnings premium," two mechanisms that the archive currently cannot distinguish because both produced positive alpha. If it prices, the whole family should be reinterpreted as an opacity-risk interaction and future refinements should target uncertainty, not accrual sign; if it fails, the cleanliness reading survives and the VOL result was a small-sample fluke.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: BuyVsBuildAccrualFinanced
evaluated.expression: MUL(RANK(RATIO(SUB(ib, oancf), at)), RANK(SUB(RATIO(DELTA(COALESCE(gdwl, 0), 1), at), RATIO(COALESCE(xrd, 0), at))))
evaluated.hypothesis: Firms that acquire their intangibles instead of building them, and whose reported income is accrual-driven, are the purest case of accounting-manufactured growth; organic innovators financed by cash earnings are the opposite corner.
evaluated.reasoning: The second leg is an explicit buy-versus-build mix (goodwill additions minus R&D intensity) rather than a level of acquired intangibles, which distinguishes it from the asset-growth proxy the critic worried about in AcquiredIntangibleAccrualFlow — a firm can score high here while shrinking assets, and low while growing them. It sharpens the archive's best short-side channel by making the intangible leg a composition variable and the accrual leg the financing condition.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: MarginBackedIntangibleAccrual
evaluated.expression: MUL(IND_RANK(RATIO(SUB(revt, cogs), revt)), RANK(NEG(WINSOR(RATIO(SUB(ib, oancf), at), 1))))
evaluated.hypothesis: Gross margin is the realized output of intangible capital — brand, patents, process knowledge — rather than its input cost; firms with industry-high margins whose earnings are cash-backed hold proven intangible capital, whereas high margins accompanied by accruals are a recognition-timing artifact.
evaluated.reasoning: Every prior intangible leg has been an input-spending measure (xrd, xad, intan), which conflates spending with productivity and excludes firms that never report R&D; using industry-ranked gross margin flips to an output-based intangible proxy with near-universal coverage. Industry ranking is essential so the leg measures firm-specific pricing power instead of sector cost structure, and pairing it with accrual cleanliness distinguishes durable margins from margins created by revenue recognition.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: IntangibleGatedWorkingCapitalBloat
evaluated.expression: MUL(IND_ZSCORE(WINSOR(RATIO(DELTA(SUB(wcap, che), 1), at), 1)), IND_RANK(RATIO(TS_SUM(COALESCE(xrd, 0), 5), at)))
evaluated.hypothesis: For firms whose real capital is intangible, a build-up of non-cash working capital is economically unjustified — innovation does not require receivables and inventory — so operating-asset bloat in an R&D-intensive firm is a direct marker of earnings created by recognition timing rather than by productive intangible investment.
evaluated.reasoning: The accrual leg is a balance-sheet working-capital construct (change in non-cash working capital) rather than the ib−oancf wedge used everywhere in the archive, so this tests whether the intangible interaction survives a completely different accrual definition and is not an artifact of cash-flow-statement mechanics. The intangible-intensity term enters as a bounded non-negative gate, so the signed bloat variable supplies the direction and the interaction predicts that identical bloat is far more damaging for an innovator than for a working-capital-intensive manufacturer.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: CashVerifiedInnovationGrowth
evaluated.expression: RATIO(SUB(DELTA(revt, 1), SUB(ib, oancf)), ADD(TS_SUM(COALESCE(xrd, 0), 5), ceq))
evaluated.hypothesis: Productive intangible investment should show up as incremental revenue that is actually collected in cash; subtracting the accrual wedge from the revenue gain and scaling by total invested capital, including the off-balance-sheet R&D stock, measures the cash-verified output of a firm's intangible capital.
evaluated.reasoning: This changes the economic quantity rather than the smoothing horizon: the numerator is an output-verification test (revenue growth net of the accruals that would make it fictitious) and the denominator is the intangible-inclusive capital base against which that output must be judged, so a firm can rank high only if its innovation spending converts into collected revenue. It is distinct from the archive's profitability ratio because it prices the incremental gain per unit of intangible capital rather than the level of gross profit, and it inherits full coverage since the denominator is never zero.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: IndustryIntangibleTechAccrual
evaluated.expression: MUL(IND_ZSCORE(WINSOR(NEG(RATIO(SUB(ib, oancf), at)), 1)), RANK(SUB(RATIO(COALESCE(xrd, 0), sale), IND_ADJ(RATIO(COALESCE(xrd, 0), sale)))))
evaluated.hypothesis: The accrual–intangible interaction may be a property of the production technology rather than of the individual filer: in intangible-intensive industries, earnings are hard to interpret for every firm, so accrual quality carries more pricing information there than in tangible industries — including for firms that report no R&D at all.
evaluated.reasoning: Subtracting the industry-demeaned R&D intensity from the raw value recovers the industry-mean intangible intensity, giving an intangible gate that is defined for every firm and therefore repairs the reporting-dummy degeneracy that broke the advertising version, while keeping the firm-level accrual signal as the signed leg. It is also a sharp economic test: if the interaction is industry-level, future refinements should condition on technology rather than on firm-reported spending; if it vanishes, the effect is firm-specific and the search should stay with own-firm intangible capital.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: OrganicMinusAcquiredIntangibleCleanAccrual
evaluated.expression: MUL(RANK(SUB(RATIO(TS_SUM(COALESCE(xrd, 0), 5), at), RATIO(COALESCE(intan, 0), at))), RANK(NEG(WINSOR(RATIO(SUB(ib, oancf), at), 1))))
evaluated.hypothesis: What matters is the origin of intangible capital: internally generated intangible stock is conservatively unrecognized and productive, whereas capitalized purchased intangibles are already priced into book value and carry impairment risk, so the organic-minus-acquired composition, conditioned on cash-backed earnings, identifies genuine hidden capital.
evaluated.reasoning: Using stock composition rather than the goodwill *flow* removes the asset-growth loading the critic flagged in the acquisition family — a stable, non-acquiring, R&D-heavy firm scores high here while a fast-growing acquirer scores low regardless of its asset growth rate. It therefore tests whether the acquisition results are about accounting origin of intangibles or merely about investment growth.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: WorkingCapitalAccrualInnovator
evaluated.expression: MUL(RANK(RATIO(TS_SUM(COALESCE(xrd, 0), 5), at)), RANK(NEG(WINSOR(RATIO(ADD(SUB(ib, oancf), dp), at), 1))))
evaluated.hypothesis: The ib−oancf wedge mixes discretionary working-capital accruals with mechanical depreciation and amortization; for intangible-intensive firms the informative part should be the discretionary working-capital component, because D&A largely reflects tangible asset age, not earnings manipulation.
evaluated.reasoning: Adding dp back to the wedge isolates the working-capital accrual and holds the intangible leg fixed at the archive's best specification, so the comparison directly attributes the winning result to a specific accrual component rather than to the aggregate. If the alpha survives or improves, the mechanism is discretionary recognition; if it collapses, the archive's effect was really a D&A/capital-intensity interaction and the search should move to the expense-treatment channel.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: AcquisitionAccrualNetAssetGrowth
evaluated.expression: MUL(RANK(RATIO(SUB(ib, oancf), at)), SUB(RANK(RATIO(DELTA(COALESCE(gdwl, 0), 1), at)), RANK(GROWTH(at, 1))))
evaluated.hypothesis: If accrual-financed acquisition of intangibles is a genuine mechanism, it should predict returns even after the firm's overall balance-sheet expansion is removed: what matters is goodwill creation in excess of general asset growth, combined with accrual-heavy earnings.
evaluated.reasoning: Subtracting the asset-growth rank from the goodwill-intensity rank orthogonalizes the intangible leg against the documented asset-growth anomaly, which is the specific attribution objection raised against the archive's strongest short-side signal. A surviving negative alpha credits purchase-accounting discretion; a vanishing one tells us to reclassify the whole acquisition family as an investment-growth effect and redirect the remaining generations to the organic/hidden-capital pole.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: EarningsDistortionFromExpensing
evaluated.expression: MUL(RANK(RATIO(COALESCE(xrd, 0), ADD(ABS(ib), COALESCE(xrd, 0)))), RANK(NEG(WINSOR(RATIO(SUB(ib, oancf), at), 1))))
evaluated.hypothesis: What determines whether expensing distorts perception is the size of R&D relative to the *earnings number investors anchor on*, not relative to assets: a firm spending as much on R&D as it reports in income has an almost meaningless earnings figure, and when its accruals are also clean the understatement is genuine and mispriced.
evaluated.reasoning: This replaces the asset-deflated intangible leg used throughout the archive with an earnings-relative distortion share bounded in [0,1], which reorders the cross-section sharply — capital-light firms with modest R&D but tiny income now rank high, while large asset-heavy R&D spenders with big profits rank low. It is a different economic claim (mispricing scales with how badly the earnings signal is corrupted, not with investment intensity) and it is not a blend of existing archive signals.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: CashCollectedTurnoverOnIntangibleCapital
evaluated.expression: RATIO(ADD(revt, recch), ADD(at, TS_SUM(COALESCE(xrd, 0), 5)))
evaluated.hypothesis: Productive intangible capital shows up as cash actually collected from customers per dollar of true invested capital; adding the receivables cash-flow adjustment strips out revenue that exists only as an accrual, and adding the R&D stock restates the capital base that generated it.
evaluated.reasoning: This repairs the earlier flawed ROE-distortion construction by building a quantity that is zero-distortion-neutral: a clean firm with no receivable build simply reports its true cash turnover, so no mechanical hidden-capital term pushes profitable innovators to the wrong extreme. Both themes are load-bearing — the numerator is accrual-purged revenue and the denominator is intangible-augmented capital — and the signal is continuous and signed, which targets the Fama-MacBeth side where the corner-product family is weakest.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: InnovatorAccrualDebtStrain
evaluated.expression: MUL(IND_ZSCORE(WINSOR(RATIO(ADD(SUB(ib, oancf), DELTA(dlc, 1)), at), 1)), IND_RANK(RATIO(COALESCE(xrd, 0), sale)))
evaluated.hypothesis: Intangible-intensive firms cannot collateralize their assets, so when reported income is accrual-supported *and* the firm is simultaneously drawing on short-term debt, the innovation program is being funded by strained external liquidity and is likely to be cut, which the market prices too late.
evaluated.reasoning: This is a financing-strain channel rather than the mirror of an existing investment-trend corner: the signed leg combines accrual earnings with short-term debt draw, and intangible intensity enters only as a bounded amplifier because the collateral problem is specific to firms whose assets are knowledge. The signed continuous leg supplies a linear cross-sectional slope while the gate concentrates the effect where the mechanism applies, so both evidence forms are addressed without recycling the R&D-trend construction.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: GrowthUnjustifiedAccrualInnovator
evaluated.expression: MUL(SUB(RANK(RATIO(DELTA(revt, 1), at)), RANK(RATIO(ADD(SUB(ib, oancf), dp), at))), RANK(RATIO(TS_SUM(COALESCE(xrd, 0), 5), at)))
evaluated.hypothesis: Only the portion of accruals that a firm's revenue expansion cannot justify is evidence of accounting-driven earnings; growing firms legitimately build working capital, so the abnormal accrual — accruals high relative to revenue growth — is the right earnings-quality input for intangible-intensive firms.
evaluated.reasoning: This inserts a Jones-style expectation model into the accrual leg using a rank difference (revenue-growth rank minus accrual rank), which keeps the two legs on a comparable bounded scale instead of subtracting variables with wildly different dispersion. It targets the diagnosis directly: the long-side family's ceiling is the crudeness of the raw accrual wedge, not the intangible measure, and abnormal accruals should separate productive investment from manipulation more sharply.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: InnovatorCashBurnAccrual
evaluated.expression: MUL(IND_ZSCORE(WINSOR(RATIO(SUB(SUB(ib, oancf), DELTA(che, 1)), at), 1)), IND_RANK(RATIO(COALESCE(xrd, 0), sale)))
evaluated.hypothesis: The strain that matters for knowledge firms is depletion of the cash buffer that funds research: an intangible-intensive firm reporting accrual-based income while its cash balance falls is consuming its only real financing capacity, and its innovation program and earnings are both unsustainable.
evaluated.reasoning: This refines the gen-3 strain result by swapping the strain proxy from short-term debt draw to cash-balance depletion, holding the gate and the signed-leg architecture fixed, so it identifies which liquidity margin actually carries the pricing information for R&D-intensive firms. Cash burn is the economically prior constraint — intangible firms typically hold cash rather than borrow — so if the debt-draw version worked, this should work at least as well and with broader applicability.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: MatureInnovationPayoffCleanAccrual
evaluated.expression: MUL(SUB(RANK(RATIO(TS_SUM(COALESCE(xrd, 0), 5), at)), RANK(RATIO(COALESCE(xrd, 0), at))), RANK(NEG(WINSOR(RATIO(SUB(ib, oancf), at), 1))))
evaluated.hypothesis: Intangible capital has a vintage: firms whose accumulated R&D stock is large relative to current-year spending are in the payoff phase, and if their earnings are cash-backed the payoff is real and unrecognized on the balance sheet, whereas ramp-phase spenders have no verified output yet.
evaluated.reasoning: Every intangible leg in the archive measures scale (stock or flow relative to assets, equity, or earnings); this measures the *stage* of the intangible program via the rank gap between accumulated stock and current outlay, which is a distinct economic state and leaves non-R&D firms neutral at zero rather than at an artificial extreme. Pairing maturity with accrual cleanliness tests whether the archive's long-side premium is compensation for unrecognized proven capital rather than for investment intensity per se.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: UnsoldInnovationInventory
evaluated.expression: MUL(IND_ZSCORE(WINSOR(RATIO(NEG(invch), at), 1)), IND_RANK(RATIO(COALESCE(xrd, 0), sale)))
evaluated.hypothesis: Inventory accumulation in a research-intensive firm is a demand-failure signal: new products that are not selling sit as inventory whose carrying value has not yet been written down, so reported earnings overstate the value of the intangible investment.
evaluated.reasoning: This isolates one specific accrual component with a mechanism unique to intangible firms — product-launch failure — rather than using the aggregate wedge, and the signed continuous leg with a bounded industry gate is the architecture that produced the best two-sided evidence in gen 3. It is a sharper economic claim than the earlier receivables-plus-inventory rank product and predicts the opposite pole (short side), which the batch otherwise underweights.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: ConsistentCashBackedInnovator
evaluated.expression: MUL(RANK(RATIO(TS_SUM(COALESCE(xrd, 0), 5), at)), RANK(TS_SUM(INDICATOR(NEG(RATIO(SUB(ib, oancf), at)), 0), 5)))
evaluated.hypothesis: For a firm whose capital is intangible, the credible quality signal is not the size of this year's accrual but the *frequency* with which earnings have been fully backed by cash: a firm that has produced cash-exceeding-earnings in most of the last five years has demonstrably productive intangible investment rather than favorable one-year working-capital timing.
evaluated.reasoning: The accrual leg becomes a discrete count of conservative-reporting years, a state variable measuring reliability rather than magnitude, which is economically different from both the one-year level and a moving average and is immune to a single outlier year driving the rank. This also changes portfolio composition materially — persistent conservatives, not firms with one large negative accrual — so it is a substantive test of whether the archive's long-side alpha reflects durable earnings quality or transitory accrual timing.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: UnderAmortizedIntangibleAccrual
evaluated.expression: MUL(RANK(RATIO(SUB(ib, oancf), at)), SUB(RANK(RATIO(COALESCE(intan, 0), at)), RANK(RATIO(dp, at))))
evaluated.hypothesis: Acquired intangibles that sit on the balance sheet without a commensurate amortization charge are unverified carrying value; when such under-amortization coincides with accrual-supported earnings, reported income is doubly overstated and will be corrected through impairment.
evaluated.reasoning: The intangible leg is now an expense-treatment mismatch — capitalized intangible intensity in excess of the firm's total D&A burden — which is neither a growth variable (the gen-3 attribution failure) nor a deflator variant of goodwill intensity, and it is well defined and stable for low- or negative-equity firms because both components are asset-scaled ranks. It targets the accounting mechanism the theme names explicitly, the expense-treatment channel, and pairs it with the accrual channel so neither leg alone can produce the signal.

evaluated.name: BalanceSheetAccrualInnovator
evaluated.expression: MUL(RANK(RATIO(TS_SUM(COALESCE(xrd, 0), 5), at)), RANK(NEG(WINSOR(RATIO(SUB(SUB(SUB(DELTA(act, 1), DELTA(che, 1)), SUB(SUB(DELTA(lct, 1), DELTA(dlc, 1)), DELTA(txp, 1))), dp), at), 1))))
evaluated.hypothesis: If the interaction reflects real accounting economics rather than an artifact of cash-flow-statement mechanics, it must hold when accruals are measured from successive balance sheets, which also extends the mechanism to the pre-cash-flow-statement era and to firms with incomplete oancf reporting.
evaluated.reasoning: Every accrual leg in the archive is built from oancf, which restricts the usable sample (coverage ~0.09) and embeds Compustat's reporting-format changes; the one signal that avoided oancf had materially higher coverage (0.113), so this is a measurement-basis and sample-length test with real power implications for ls_talpha. It is not a cosmetic change: the balance-sheet definition captures working-capital accruals including non-cash items that never pass through oancf, and disagreement between the two versions would localize the mechanism.

considered.expression: MUL(RANK(RATIO(COALESCE(intan, 0), at)), RANK(WINSOR(SUB(RATIO(SUB(SUB(act, che), SUB(lct, dlc)), sale), MA(RATIO(SUB(SUB(act, che), SUB(lct, dlc)), sale), 5)), 1)))
considered.hypothesis: A firm carrying a large purchased-intangible balance whose working capital has also drifted above its own historical requirement is overstating both its long-term assets and its current earnings, and both overstatements unwind.
considered.reasoning: The short side of this study has relied on acquisition *flows* (goodwill growth, Δintan), which the gen-3 attribution test showed are contaminated by asset growth; using the acquired-intangible stock together with the within-firm working-capital deviation removes every growth-rate input from the signal, so a surviving negative alpha cannot be attributed to the investment anomaly. It also gives the batch a short-side test built from the two components that proved most robust on coverage and Sharpe rather than another pass at buy-versus-build.

considered.name: NonResearchOverheadConservatism
considered.expression: MUL(RANK(RATIO(SUB(SUB(SUB(revt, cogs), ib), COALESCE(xrd, 0)), at)), RANK(NEG(WINSOR(RATIO(SUB(SUB(SUB(DELTA(act, 1), DELTA(che, 1)), SUB(SUB(DELTA(lct, 1), DELTA(dlc, 1)), DELTA(txp, 1))), dp), at), 1))))
considered.hypothesis: Organizational, human and brand capital are built through overhead spending that is expensed with no disclosure line of its own; removing reported R&D from the gross-profit-minus-net-income gap isolates precisely this undisclosed investment, and where it is large and accruals are clean, earnings understate economic capital.
considered.reasoning:
Every intangible leg in the archive is either disclosed R&D, disclosed advertising, or purchased intangibles, so the study cannot currently say whether the conservatism premium exists for the majority of firms that invest without an R&D line; subtracting xrd makes the leg orthogonal to the entire R&D family rather than a redeflation of it. It has near-universal coverage and, paired with the balance-sheet accrual, keeps the productive-versus-accounting separation while testing the mechanism in a population the study has never reached.

considered.name: RisingExpensedInvestmentVsOwnNorm
considered.expression: MUL(RANK(WINSOR(SUB(RATIO(SUB(SUB(revt, cogs), ib), at), MA(RATIO(SUB(SUB(revt, cogs), ib), at), 5)), 1)), RANK(NEG(WINSOR(RATIO(SUB(SUB(SUB(DELTA(act, 1), DELTA(che, 1)), SUB(SUB(DELTA(lct, 1), DELTA(dlc, 1)), DELTA(txp, 1))), dp), at), 1))))
considered.hypothesis: A firm currently expensing more investment than its own five-year norm has depressed earnings for investment reasons rather than for operating reasons, and when the accrual base is simultaneously clean the depressed earnings are unambiguously conservative rather than managed.
considered.reasoning:
All intangible legs tested so far are cross-sectional levels, which conflate business model with investment behaviour; the deviation of expensed investment intensity from the firm's own norm identifies firms whose *current* reported earnings are temporarily understated, which is the state in which earnings-anchored mispricing should be largest. Both legs are firm-relative or peer-relative in different ways, so the interaction is not a re-weighting of the archive's level-times-level structure.

considered.name: CustomerPrepaymentKnowledgeFirms
considered.expression: MUL(RANK(RATIO(COALESCE(xrd, 0), ADD(COALESCE(xrd, 0), dp))), RANK(WINSOR(SUB(GROWTH(SUB(lct, dlc), 1), GROWTH(sale, 1)), 1)))
considered.hypothesis: The liability side of working capital carries the opposite signal from the asset side: non-debt current liabilities growing faster than sales means customers and suppliers are financing the firm — deferred revenue and accrued expenses rather than receivables — which for knowledge-intensive firms indicates cash collected ahead of recognized revenue.
considered.reasoning:
Every accrual construct in this study treats non-debt current liabilities only as a subtraction inside a net working-capital aggregate, so the study has never tested the liability channel on its own, and its economics for subscription- and contract-based intangible businesses is the mirror image of the receivable channel: prepayment is conservative, not aggressive. The leg is unit-matched (two growth rates), requires no cash-flow-statement data, and predicts a sign opposite to the naive accrual reading, making the test genuinely discriminating.

considered.name: WeakestLinkOverheadAccrual
considered.expression: MIN(RANK(RATIO(SUB(SUB(revt, cogs), ib), at)), RANK(NEG(WINSOR(RATIO(SUB(SUB(SUB(DELTA(act, 1), DELTA(che, 1)), SUB(SUB(DELTA(lct, 1), DELTA(dlc, 1)), DELTA(txp, 1))), dp), at), 1))))
considered.hypothesis: Understated earnings are only informative when they are also credible, so a firm should be credited by the weaker of two conditions — how much investment it expenses and how free of accruals its balance sheet is — with no compensation between them.
considered.reasoning:
The gen-8 weakest-link test produced the study's best cross-sectional slope (4.33) but weak alpha, and the diagnosis is specific: the alpha loss came from the third, margin-level channel, which has destroyed alpha in every specification it has entered, not from the conjunctive form itself. Applying the same form to two channels only — one of which is the new expensed-investment leg — is the decisive test of that diagnosis and, if correct, should deliver a high slope together with the family's usual 5–6% alpha.

critic_notes.rationale: The rank product genuinely isolates the joint high-R&D/low-accrual corner rather than re-labeling either sort, and sign logic is internally consistent, but it remains a fairly standard two-anomaly (Sloan accruals × R&D intensity) intersection whose incremental content over each parent is modest.

This is the standard accrual anomaly with a cosmetically enlarged deflator — the numerator, cross-sectional ranking, and expected sign are all Sloan (1996), so the R&D stock in the denominator only mildly rescales a known signal rather than creating a distinct cross-theme mechanism.

Adding negative accruals and R&D intensity in raw (unstandardized) units on a common deflator is a mechanical sum of two published anomalies whose relative weight is set arbitrarily by their dispersion (accruals will dominate), and it duplicates the economic content of CashFundedInnovation and IndustryNeutralInnovationMinusAccrual in this same batch.

Using acquired-intangible intensity as a non-negative intensity weight on signed accruals is a coherent, sign-consistent conditional interaction with a specific accounting mechanism (purchase-accounting discretion) that is not spanned by either parent sort, though the large mass of zero-goodwill firms will pile near zero and should be monitored for unstable portfolio composition.

Framing the signal in changes (R&D acceleration versus accrual change) is a substantively different construction from the level-based parents and the expected sign matches the expression, but second differences of xrd/sale are very noisy and DELTA of accruals is close to an earnings-acceleration proxy, so expect weak power despite the sound design.

Industry z-scoring is a legitimate refinement and the units are properly comparable, but the signal is an equal-weight difference of two well-known anomalies and carries essentially the same economic content as CashFundedInnovation and ConservatismCashEarningsGap in this batch, making it redundant rather than novel.

This is a cosmetic recombination of two already-evaluated archive constructs (CashGrossProfitOnIntangibleCapital plus the raw R&D-intensity leg of CashFundedInnovation) with no new economic mechanism, and the stated motivation is explicitly metric-chasing — averaging a strong-FMB/weak-alpha leg with a strong-alpha/weak-FMB leg rather than diagnosing why they disagree.

Decomposing the accrual wedge into the receivables/inventory component that actually plausibly interacts with new-product revenue recognition is a substantively different design question from gen 0, and the sign logic is correct given Compustat's decrease(increase) convention for recch/invch — though coverage will be limited to post-1988 cash-flow-format firms and the zero-R&D mass will compress one leg.

The stock-to-flow switch and double-ranking are a defensible response to the compressed short leg in GoodwillWeightedAccrualAggression and the expected negative sign matches the expression, but it remains the same accrual×acquired-intangible interaction family and the Δintan leg risks simply proxying the known asset-growth/investment anomaly.

The hypothesis is about mispricing relative to earnings-anchored valuation but the expression contains no price or valuation multiple, so it cannot test understatement; mechanically it is a capital-intensity (dp/at) sort gated on intangible intensity, and dp is dominated by tangible depreciation, which plausibly predicts the opposite sign.

The second-moment accrual-reliability channel is a genuinely new axis for this pair and yields a falsifiable sign flip, but accrual volatility is close to the published Dechow-Dichev/earnings-volatility anomaly, the 5-observation annual VOL is noisy, and the negative expected sign fights the positive R&D-intensity leg embedded in the product.

TS_COUNT(xrd,5) is a near-binary, tie-saturated R&D-reporter dummy that will degenerate entirely if xrd is coalesced/zero-filled upstream, so the signal reduces largely to the classic Sloan accrual anomaly measured within R&D reporters rather than a new intangible-commitment channel.

This is a cosmetic merge of two archive signals (CashFundedInnovation and HiddenEquityCleanAccruals) that differ only in deflator, and the outer RANK is a monotone transform that cannot change decile membership at all, so it adds no new economic content and only re-scales the Fama-MacBeth regressor.

Replacing signed accruals with |accruals| is a legitimate, sign-discriminating test of the opacity-premium reading suggested by IntangibleAccrualInstability's flipped result, though ABS(accrual) and VOL(accrual) are highly correlated so it risks being a near-duplicate of that archive entry, and the positive expected sign should be pre-committed rather than fitted after the fact.

The buy-versus-build composition leg is a genuine construction change relative to AcquiredIntangibleAccrualFlow and the sign logic is internally consistent, but goodwill growth remains heavily loaded on the well-documented acquisition/asset-growth anomaly, so any result needs an asset-growth control to be credited to the accrual mechanism.

Swapping a one-year accrual for a three-year moving average of the same accrual, with the intangible leg held identical to the archive winner, is a smoothing tweak rather than a new mechanism, and it also silently drops the WINSOR used in the comparable archive signals so the comparison is not even clean.

The external-validity motivation is sound, but COALESCE(xad,0) makes the RANK leg mostly a reporting indicator (a large majority of firms tie at zero), so the interaction degenerates into "advertiser dummy × clean accruals" on a sparse population, and advertising intensity is itself a published return predictor.

Multiplying two of the best-known published anomalies (gross profitability and accruals) is close to a mechanical two-factor composite rather than a novel mechanism, but the industry ranking and the near-universal coverage relative to the archive's 0.09 make it a worthwhile robustness test of whether the effect is intangible-specific or just profitability × earnings quality.

This is a mechanical rank-blend of two already-evaluated archive signals (the R&D-stock × clean-accrual corner and the goodwill-flow × dirty-accrual corner from BuyVsBuildAccrualFinanced / AcquiredIntangibleAccrualFlow), so it tests ensembling rather than a new economic mechanism and its alpha will be a near-deterministic average of results already known.

A defensible reframing of the buy-vs-build family that swaps the acquisition *flow* (asset-growth-contaminated) for a balance-sheet *stock* composition, though it overlaps materially with BuyVsBuildAccrualFinanced and the raw difference of two differently-scaled ratios before ranking is a crude composition measure.

The expression correctly isolates the working-capital component of the wedge (ib − oancf + dp ≈ ΔWC less other non-cash items) and the sign logic is internally consistent, but it is a component decomposition of the archive's best specification that partially duplicates InnovationWorkingCapitalDiscipline and reverts to essentially the canonical Sloan accrual definition.

Internally inconsistent: for a clean firm with ib = oancf the expression still equals ib·R/(ceq(ceq+R)) > 0, so profitable, cash-backed, R&D-heavy firms — precisely the population the archive finds *underpriced* — land at the short extreme, meaning the mechanical hidden-capital term fights the stated accrual story and the expected negative sign.

A legitimate and clearly falsifiable attribution test of whether the acquisition-accrual result is distinct from the asset-growth anomaly, with the caveat that a rank difference is not real orthogonalization and the embedded low-asset-growth tilt pushes against the expected negative sign, biasing the test toward rejection.

Despite the disclaimer, MUL(RANK(NEG(trend)), RANK(accrual)) ≈ (1−a)(1−b) is the mirror corner of SustainedRnDRampCleanAccruals' ab and is negatively correlated with it, so with a negative expected sign this is effectively a sign-flipped restatement of an already-tested, weak-alpha signal.

This is a pure functional-form re-wrapping of the archived WorkingCapitalAccrualInnovator (identical two rank legs, MIN instead of MUL), and since MIN and the rank product are near-monotonically related in the extreme deciles that drive the long-short spread, it is a cosmetic variant unlikely to produce economically distinct evidence.

The Jones-style "accruals unjustified by revenue growth" refinement is a substantive change to the earnings-quality leg rather than a cosmetic one, but the rank-difference construction imports raw revenue growth with a *positive* loading, which fights the well-documented growth/asset-growth anomaly and muddies attribution between abnormal accruals and plain growth.

Swapping short-term-debt draw for cash-balance depletion is a defensible test of which liquidity margin carries the pricing information, and the sign convention is internally consistent, but summing an accrual wedge and Δcash into one scalar is conceptually impure since Δche is driven mainly by financing and investing flows rather than earnings quality.

Measuring the *stage* rather than the scale of the intangible program is a genuinely distinct state variable that leaves non-reporters neutral, though the rank gap between the 5-year stock and current flow is largely an inverse R&D-growth proxy and therefore points in the opposite direction to the archived SustainedRnDRamp signal while carrying the same expected sign — a tension the test should be designed to resolve.

Isolating the inventory component with a launch-failure mechanism is a sharper claim than the earlier receivables-plus-inventory product and the invch sign convention is handled correctly, but the design risks being degenerate exactly where the gate is strongest, since the most R&D-intensive firms (biotech, software) typically carry negligible inventory.

This is essentially the gen-0 GoodwillWeightedAccrualAggression with the goodwill deflator changed from assets to book equity plus industry wrappers — the cited gen-3 attribution failure applied to the goodwill *flow*, not the stock — and gdwl/ceq is unstable or sign-flipping for the low- and negative-equity firms that are precisely the most impairment-vulnerable cases.

This is essentially an ensemble of two already-evaluated archive signals (ConsistentCashBackedInnovator's five-year conservatism count and WorkingCapitalAccrualInnovator's ib−oancf+dp leg) sharing an identical intangible leg, so it recombines existing results rather than testing a new economic mechanism, and the SUMRANK blend will mechanically inherit an intermediate slope/alpha with no diagnostic value.

The balance-sheet accrual definition is the canonical Sloan (1996) measure rather than anything new, and the interaction partner is unchanged from the archive's strongest long-side signal, but as a measurement-basis and sample-coverage robustness test it is internally consistent (NEG makes low accruals high, matching the positive expected sign) and could plausibly change power rather than just cosmetics.

The signed direction is correct (NEG(aoloch) rising means a build-up of net other operating assets, predicting low returns) and the "other/soft" accrual component is a genuinely untested leg here, but the stated economics is partly wrong — capitalized software and development costs typically flow through investing activities, not aoloch — so the component is closer to a generic Richardson-style low-reliability accrual bucket than to the expense-treatment story claimed.

Replacing the generic accrual leg with a deterioration trigger is a substantive change of mechanism rather than a re-weighting, and the sign logic holds (high intan-minus-dp rank spread times high deterioration rank yields the most negative expected returns), though the under-amortization proxy remains contaminated because dp includes tangible depreciation, so PP&E-heavy firms will be mislabeled as "over-amortized."

The within-firm accrual position is a defensible way to strip firm-specific accounting norms from the level, and the sign is coherent, but it overlaps meaningfully with the already-evaluated AccrualInnovationRotation (TS_RANK of the same accrual wedge) and IntangibleAccrualInstability, so the incremental information is a gating/scaling change more than a new mechanism.

This is WorkingCapitalAccrualInnovator with both legs re-scaled from RANK to IND_RANK and nothing else changed — the archetypal cosmetic variant — and the industry-attribution question it claims to answer is already partly addressed by the archive's several IND_ZSCORE/IND_RANK-gated versions of the same accrual–intangible pair.

It is a mechanical cross of two archive signals (the conservatism-frequency count and the balance-sheet accrual definition), but the resulting variable — a five-year reliability state measured without oancf — is economically distinct, correctly signed, and directly tests whether persistence and magnitude were traded off by measurement rather than economics.

Summing Sloan accruals over three years is close to the published net-operating-assets/accrual-persistence anomaly and will be highly correlated with the gen-5 one-year winner, but the flow-versus-stock distinction is a legitimate and cleanly specified test rather than a cosmetic re-scaling, and the sign convention is internally consistent.

The continuous leg (at − che − lct + dlc)/at is essentially the published net-operating-assets anomaly of Hirshleifer–Hou–Teoh–Zhang, and because che dominates its cross-sectional variation the signal will largely rank cash-rich R&D firms, making the "interaction" mechanically confounded with cash holdings rather than an independent accrual mechanism.

This is a cosmetic RANK→IND_RANK substitution on the existing ImpairmentTriggerUnderAmortized, and the stated repair does not work — industry ranking does not remove within-industry PP&E-intensity variation in dp, whereas a substantive fix would scale amortization by intan or use an amortization-specific item.

The hypothesis (income validated by taxes actually owed to an outside authority) contradicts what the expression computes, since txp is the unpaid balance-sheet accrued-tax liability — a positive accrual whose growth signals deferral, not verification — and ABS(ib) in the denominator maps profitable and loss firms to the same value, destroying the intended interpretation.

A predictably high-correlation redefinition of the gen-5 winner's intangible leg, but the hidden-capital hypothesis genuinely implies advertising should belong there and the test is discriminating; the main risk is that COALESCE(xad,0) makes the change nearly inert for R&D reporters while adding pure advertisers as noise.

The Hribar–Collins-style balance-sheet accrual re-measurement is a legitimate, sign-consistent power upgrade applied to the archive's largest-alpha leg (buy-vs-build), but it is a one-dimensional measurement swap with no new economics, and the identical swap appears three times in this batch, so at most one such test is informative.

Internally consistent (NEG on the accrual leg correctly makes clean accruals the long side) and the R&D-disclosure-independent margin leg is a real advantage, though the construction is essentially gross-profitability × accruals — two well-known standalone anomalies — recombined with a measurement tweak on an already-archived variant.

The claimed reordering is illusory because x/(ceq+x) is a monotone transform of x/ceq for all positive-equity firms, so RANK is unchanged except for the handful of negative-equity cases, leaving this a near-duplicate of the archived HiddenEquityCleanAccruals plus the batch's boilerplate accrual swap.

This is the batch's most substantive construction — a properly unit-matched working-capital-growth-minus-sales-growth residual interacted with intangible intensity, with the expected negative sign matching the expression's direction — though GROWTH(act−che) can be unstable when non-cash current assets are near zero and the leg is cousin to the asset-growth anomaly.

Replacing the archived level of the working-capital cycle with its five-year trend asks a genuine state-versus-drift question and correctly differences out stable business-model differences, but it is a close temporal variant of an already-tested leg and the 5-year estimator will cost coverage and stability.

This is the third instance of the same balance-sheet-accrual substitution applied to an already-archived signal (OrganicMinusAcquiredIntangibleCleanAccrual), adds no variation to the intangible leg that the archive has not already seen, and is mislabeled as "composite" when it is plainly a conditional interaction.

The construction is internally consistent and correctly signed, but it is a purely mechanical "best-slope leg × best-alpha leg" recombination of two archived signals with no new economic content, and the two accrual-quality legs are likely to be substantially redundant (note also the original's within-industry standardization of the working-capital residual is silently dropped, so any change may reflect that rather than the pairing).

A legitimate flow-versus-stock robustness test of the gen-7 knowledge-share result with a clearly stated economic reading, though it sits close to the already-mined HiddenEquityCleanAccruals / R&D-stock × clean-accrual family, and the denominator term (at − act − intan) can go negative or near-zero for asset-light firms, which can invert or explode the ratio and should be guarded.

This is the third pass at the same buy-versus-build × accrual interaction (after BuyVsBuildAccrualFinanced and BuyVsBuildBalanceSheetAccrual), differing only in which accrual proxy is plugged into the second leg — a cosmetic variant chosen by metric arithmetic rather than a new mechanism.

The stated reasoning claims to cumulate both legs of the gen-7 signal, but the R&D leg is silently changed from a one-year change to a three-year stock level, which converts the expression into a difference-form restatement of the already-tested CumulativeAccrualBloatInnovator (R&D stock × 3-year cumulative accruals) rather than the horizon test it advertises.

The hypothesis requires three conditions to hold *simultaneously*, but a product of three ranks is compensatory rather than conjunctive (a very high margin rank can offset a poor accrual rank), so the expression does not test the stated claim; it also risks being a diluted, more skewed version of the already-strong gen-7 knowledge-share × clean-accrual signal whose pairwise components are all previously tested.

A genuinely new leg (second-moment margin stability rather than margin level) motivated by a specific, credible diagnosis of the margin-level signal's poor Sharpe, correctly signed and disclosure-independent — though it overlaps conceptually with published quality/earnings-stability factors, so the incremental content over a QMJ-style stability control should be checked.

The two "independent" discretion footprints are both built from the same non-cash working-capital aggregate (act−che minus lct−dlc components), so their errors are far from independent and the signal is largely a re-weighted blend of two already-archived winners (gen-7 ls_talpha 6.43, gen-8 6.01) rather than a substantively new mechanism.

This changes only the deflator (at → MA(at,3)) on the archived gen-7 KnowledgeShareOfCapitalProgramCleanAccrual, which is precisely the kind of cosmetic re-scaling variant the objective warns against, and MA(at,3) is not even the literature's t/t−1 average-asset convention.

Economically coherent and sign-consistent, but it is a straight recombination of two already-tested legs (gen-8 KnowledgeStockShareCleanAccrual and gen-8 AbnormalWorkingCapitalVsOwnNormInnovator) whose expected marginal information is small given both share the same knowledge-capital and working-capital constructs.

A pure operator-form re-expression of the gen-7 product signal that also duplicates the already-archived difference-form family (InvisibleVersusAccrualExpansion, ThreeYearExpansionChannelContrast), and by construction it abandons the conditional interaction the theme is meant to test in favor of an additive two-factor blend.

A genuinely disclosure-independent intangible proxy that broadens coverage, but (revt−cogs−ib)/at mechanically rises with low or negative net income (and with interest/tax burden), so it partly proxies unprofitability rather than expensed investment and overlaps the published SG&A/organization-capital anomaly — worth testing only with that confound explicitly diagnosed.

Sign and construction are internally consistent and the growth-free design is a legitimate response to the earlier flow-based contamination critique, though both legs are recycled from archived signals and the acquired-intangible *level* has weak standalone motivation for negative drift absent an impairment trigger.
